title: A message signed V. Carranza, transcribed by Capt. A. H. Castañeda for Gral. P. González, undated [probably May 1914] (catalogue 1465): eight coded runs in Clave Extra 3 read in part with the key rebuilt from the pencil decipherment of LXVIII-1.14.1943.1 (52 of 61 coded words verbatim)

documents.shelfmark: Mexico City, CEHM-Carso (Centro de Estudios de Historia de México, Fundación Carlos Slim), Fondo LXVIII-1 (Manuscritos del General Manuel Willars González [Pablo González]), LXVIII-1.23.3165.1
documents.date: undated; probably May 1914 (inferred from the orders on Saltillo)
documents.route: Capt. A. H. Castañeda, transcribing a message signed V. Carranza -> Gral. P. González

plaintext.source: Bare coded runs; no decipherment on the sheet. Key: Clave Extra 3, rebuilt from LXVIII-1.14.1943.1 (same fondo; targets/murguia1914).

transcription.notes: Pencil, right half faint, a large loop and a vertical line drawn across. Two passes without the key (1600 px overview; fresh half-width crops enlarged 1.2-1.3x with contrast stretch): same group at 209 of 235 places, the 26 differences settled on the crops where possible; 8 groups keep an unread figure; distinct counts the 41 fully read groups. Blind check by the reviewer: every legible group of 47 agrees.

system.summary: Clave Extra 3 (so named on LXVIII-1.14.1943.1). Two-figure groups 10-99 in a table read by the units figure: tens 1/2 = a0 b9 c8 d7 e6 f5 g4 h3 i2 j1; tens 3/4 = l0 ll9 m8 n7 ñ6 o5 p4 q3 r2 rr1; tens 5/6 = s0 t9 u8 v7 y4 z3 (51 -mente); 7x-9x are word groups (78 por, 82 enemigo, 87 para, 90 parque, 91 la, 96 de, 99 que; 88 and 97 not identified). The layout gives each letter two homophones, one per tens figure of its pair.
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the 62 cells of the Clave Extra 3 key (key_frozen.tsv holds the 60 with a value); 41 distinct fully read groups occur on this sheet, the word groups 13 times as 4 distinct groups (82, 87, 96, 99). Groups are joined by hyphens; runs are separated by clear words.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment on the sheet; the key comes from LXVIII-1.14.1943.1 (targets/murguia1914). No edition found (web searches 12-13 Nov 2026; Narváez 2019 and 2025 and M. W. González, Con Carranza, not read).

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 1465) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed the figures twice, built or fitted and froze the key, decrypted, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (decryption, mark check, word count)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), viewing the images

solution.what: LXVIII-1.2.56.1, 2.75.1, 7.890.1, 14.1943.1 (4 pages), 17.2435.1, 23.3148.1 and 23.3165.1 fetched from the CEHM image server one at a time, 2 s apart; 8.957.1-2 returned 404.

Pencil, right half faint, a large loop and a vertical line drawn across. Two passes without the key (1600 px overview; fresh half-width crops enlarged 1.2-1.3x with contrast stretch): same group at 209 of 235 places, the 26 differences settled on the crops where possible; 8 groups keep an unread figure; distinct counts the 41 fully read groups. Blind check by the reviewer: every legible group of 47 agrees.

Clave Extra 3 key (targets/murguia1914/key_frozen.tsv, 60 entries) rebuilt from the contemporary pencil decipherment of LXVIII-1.14.1943.1 and frozen before this sheet was decrypted; copied unchanged into this folder. This sheet was not used to build or test the key.

Decrypted mechanically with key_frozen.tsv and read as sentences with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py passes (8 runs, 10 marks, 0 failures). 61 coded words: 52 verbatim, 2 with a marked repair, 7 with a guess for a group whose figures are not legible (8 groups). Per run verbatim: C01 9/11, C02 8/9, C03 5/5, C04 7/7, C05 6/6, C06 8/11, C07 4/6, C08 5/6.

Web searches (Pablo González 1913-1914 clave; cifrados constitucionalistas; Narváez, 'Algunos casos criptográficos del movimiento constitucionalista, 1914-1915', Historia Mexicana 75/2, 2025), repeated once by the reviewer on 13 Nov: no edition or decipherment of these documents or of Clave Extra 3. Narváez 2025 (403 to a script) and 2019, and M. W. González, Con Carranza (1933-34), not read.

Independent blind review by a second AI language-model agent (13 Nov 2026): every legible group of 47 checked agrees on its own crops (C02 g14 confirmed as 42 on a 3x zoom; a stroke in C01 confirmed as a descender, not a group); scripts reproduced; reading graded B.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py on validation.tsv, the mechanical values of the frozen key per group; scripts/validation_pairs.py): 227 read tokens, 41 types, es-modern order 4: reading -2.317 per letter; random keys mean -6.136, max -4.722 (z 7.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.978 (mean -3.122, z 8.1); annealer on the real text -2.828. Verdict: pass.

Integration check (13 Nov 2026): own decoder from key_frozen.tsv (nothing imported) gives the same eight lines; scripts and docs/_validate.py re-run with the same figures (52 of 61 verbatim; z 7.3, pass); key_frozen.tsv equals targets/murguia1914/key_frozen.tsv (PR #513) line for line. The freezing order rests on the contributor's record (one commit). The reading names Saltillo, Villa, Coss, Eulalio Gutiérrez and San Luis.

Integration check (13 Nov 2026): CEHM image LXVIII-1.23.3165.1.0001 fetched over plain http (no refusal); runs C01-C03, C06 and C07 compared at full resolution, about 100 groups: every legible group agrees, the open figures are as transcribed (C06 g14 looks like an open 99). Strict share confirmed: 52 of 61 coded words verbatim (85.2%), read in part.

texts.label: Carranza message on Villa and Saltillo, [probably May 1914]
texts.summary: Forces of 'esta División' are to move on Saltillo; González is to send one of the chiefs at Monterrey to cooperate in the operations under the immediate orders of General Villa; General Coss is to stand south of Saltillo on the enemy's line of retreat and attack him as he leaves, in concert with General Eulalio Gutiérrez on the Saltillo-San Luis line. The date (probably May 1914) is inferred.
texts.note: 61 coded words in 8 runs: 52 verbatim from the signs (85.2%), 2 with a marked repair ({+l}as, c{f/o}n), 7 with a guess for an unread group: 5 one-letter guesses, 2 letters in pertenecientes, and the word 'que' for ?9. The clear head of the message is partly faint.

reading_review.note: Coherent orders: move on Saltillo, a chief from Monterrey under Villa, Coss south of Saltillo on the enemy's retreat, in concert with Eulalio Gutiérrez on the Saltillo-San Luis line. Seven words have a guess for an unread pencil figure, each forced by the word; the clear head is partly faint and the May 1914 date is an inference, labelled as one.

gaps.item: 8 groups with an unread figure (C01 g9, g13, g36; C06 g14, g31; C07 g10, g25; C08 g15)
gaps.detail: Faint pencil or under the drawn loop; the reading guesses a value for each, marked.

gaps.item: The clear head of the message ('fechado ayer en S[...]')
gaps.detail: Not fully read; no governing verb read before 'a esta División a moverse'.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.317; polyphony 0.0; 8 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.828
